text.brief: A soybean farmer in Iowa learns in 2044 that the drought-tolerant seed his county has planted for five years carries a license that expires at season's end. The owner is a mainland firm, and renewal waits on a trade dispute.
text.record: ChemChina bought the seed and crop chemical company Syngenta for $43 billion in 2017. Arkansas ordered Syngenta Seeds in October 2023 to sell 160 acres of farmland and later collected a $280,000 fine. The USDA counted 247,659 acres of American farmland held by Chinese investors at the end of 2024 ([USDA, Foreign Holdings of U.S. Agricultural Land through December 31, 2024](https://www.fsa.usda.gov/sites/default/files/2026-01/AFIDAYR2024ReportWithPageNumbers.pdf)).
text.reading: The Party lures American farms onto its seeds, then holds the ladder. AI-designed traits outperform, and a license rather than a gun decides the next planting. This is Stratagem 28, lure the enemy onto the roof and remove the ladder.
text.coreEvent: The Party restricts American access to a mainland-owned seed line or animal vaccine during a dispute before 2045.
text.gapText: Business Architecture. Farmers buy seed on price and yield, and no one prices the season a license holder says no.
text.fix: Keep public breeding strong and escrow critical genetics, so every seed line has a fallback.
